title: 学习与教育词汇
goal: 理解学习与教育词汇及学习过程与效果的描述。

points.label: 理解教育话题词汇的语境义
读懂学习过程与效果的描述

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲（2016年修订版）

body.p: 本课词汇分为三组。第一组是学习过程，如注意、理解、练习和复习。第二组是教学活动，如解释、示范和反馈。第三组是学习效果，通常通过作业和评价来观察。
记词时连同词性和搭配一起记，它们决定词在句中的用法。例如 pay attention to 表示注意，feedback on a draft 表示对草稿的反馈。

body.box: Nora studies a little each evening. She first tries to recall the main ideas without looking at her notes. Then she checks what she missed and reviews that part. On Fridays she explains an idea to a classmate, who asks questions and gives feedback. When a question reveals a mistake, Nora returns to the relevant material. Her schedule leaves time for practice as well as checking, and she adjusts it when an exercise takes longer than expected.

body.p: recall 指先凭记忆回想，review 指随后复习漏掉的部分。feedback 指同学提出的问题和意见。问题暴露出错误后，Nora 回头重读相关的材料。

groups.fill: A class keeps a record of its reading. Students pay atte{ntion} to the main idea and take no{tes} on details. They rev{iew} their notes after class. Each student can ask a ques{tion} about a passage. A teacher may give an exa{mple} to explain an unfamiliar idea. Students then complete an exer{cise} and check for a mis{take}. The teacher gives feed{back} on their answers. Over time, students can see their prog{ress} and gain confi{dence} in reading.
notes: attention：pay attention to 表示注意。
question：ask a question 表示提问。
example：例子用于解释生疏的概念。
exercise：complete an exercise 表示完成练习题。
confidence：gain confidence 表示增强信心。

groups.text: A class mapped the routes people use to reach a community center. First, students walked along the nearby streets and noted crossings and bus stops. They compared their notes in groups and found that some routes had no safe crossing close to the center. The teacher asked each group to draw a map and explain its choices. When the groups compared their maps, they noticed that one map omitted a bus stop. The students returned to their notes and added it. They also agreed on symbols for crossings and stops, so that readers could understand the maps without asking the students for help. Each group wrote a short explanation beside its map. The explanations described what the students had observed during their walks. The teacher assessed whether the maps showed the routes clearly, not whether every group had drawn them in the same style. The class then gave copies to the center. The staff could use the maps to discuss possible changes, although the class did not decide which changes would be made. The students kept their original notes in the classroom for later reference.

items.stem: What did students record during their walks?
options: Crossings and bus stops
Drawings and teaching styles
Changes already made by staff
Questions from center visitors
items.why: 依据是 noted crossings and bus stops，即第一项。

items.stem: Why did one group add a bus stop to its map?
options: The teacher had changed the routes.
A comparison revealed it was missing.
The center had built a new stop.
The class had chosen one drawing style.
items.why: 依据是 When the groups compared their maps, they noticed that one map omitted a bus stop。比较地图时发现漏了车站，学生查看笔记后补上，即第二项。

options: Whether every map used the same style
Whether the center changed its routes
Whether the routes were shown clearly
Whether students chose the final changes
items.why: 依据是 assessed whether the maps showed the routes clearly。

items.stem: What could the center staff do with the maps?
options: Replace the students' walking notes
Require a single drawing style
Assess how clearly routes were shown
Discuss possible route changes
items.why: 依据是 The staff could use the maps to discuss possible changes，即第四项。第三项是教师做的事，不是中心工作人员。

items.stem: Which action came before drawing the maps?
options: Comparing notes about the streets
Deciding the center's final changes
Giving finished maps to the center
Assessing the clarity of the maps
items.why: 学生先 walked along the nearby streets 并 compared their notes，随后绘图。

groups.fill: A teacher asked a class to prepare short talks. Each student chose a topic and made a study sche{dule}. They read mate{rial} and took notes on the main ideas. Before speaking, they had time to prac{tice}. A partner listened and gave feed{back} on the first version. Students used an exa{mple} to make an idea clear. The teacher asked a ques{tion} after each talk. Students checked one mis{take} and planned how to imp{rove}. The final asses{sment} considered clear explanations as well as accurate facts. Students could see their prog{ress} by comparing versions.

groups.text:
Lea wanted to understand the ideas in a set of history readings, but her first routine left her with pages of notes and little time to check them. She often copied sentences while reading. Later, when she looked at the notes, she could not always tell which details supported the main argument. She decided to change one part of her routine.

After each short section, Lea closed the book and wrote a few sentences from memory. Then she reopened it and compared her account with the text. If she had missed a connection between events, she added it in a different color. She kept her original account as well, so that she could see what she had remembered before checking. The aim was to find gaps in understanding, rather than to produce a perfect account on the first attempt.

Once a week Lea discussed one reading with a classmate. They asked each other for evidence behind their explanations. When their accounts differed, they returned to the relevant paragraph instead of assuming that the longer account was correct. This process took time, so Lea chose fewer readings for each session. She used the extra time to check her explanations and revise the notes that needed work.

items.stem: What difficulty did Lea have with her first notes?
options: They did not clearly show how details supported the argument.
They gave too much time for checking the main argument.
They contained no sentences from the history readings.
They separated every detail from the reading it described.
items.why: 依据是 could not always tell which details supported the main argument。

items.stem: What did Lea do immediately after each short section?
options: She discussed the reading with her classmate.
She wrote a brief account from memory.
She copied the relevant paragraph in color.
She compared the longer and shorter accounts.
items.why: 依据是 closed the book and wrote a few sentences from memory。

items.stem: Why did Lea keep her original account?
options: To avoid adding missed connections later
To show that the first account was perfect
To see what she recalled before checking
To give her classmate a longer explanation
items.why: 依据是 see what she had remembered before checking。

items.stem: What did Lea and her classmate do when their accounts differed?
options: They chose the account with more details.
They stopped discussing that reading.
They added the missing link in color.
They checked the paragraph concerned.
items.why: 依据是 they returned to the relevant paragraph，第四项用 the paragraph concerned 改写了 the relevant paragraph。第一项正是原文否定的做法。

items.stem: Why did Lea choose fewer readings per session?
options: To leave time to check and revise explanations
To replace her written account with copied notes
To avoid asking for evidence during discussions
To compare more accounts without reading again
items.why: 依据是 This process took time 和 used the extra time to check her explanations and revise the notes，即第一项。
